bull.b: Growing Elfabrio sales and broader dosing and geographic approvals can deepen product adoption and extend commercial reach. The partner-led model enables expansion without requiring Protalix to build a large direct sales infrastructure, supporting durable revenue potential in Fabry disease.

Positive earnings, strong operating margins, and a debt-free balance sheet give Protalix greater financial flexibility to fund operations and advance its pipeline. Current cash generation and liquidity also reduce dependence on external financing while commercial programs develop.

Progressing PRX-115 through a multiple-dose Phase 2 study provides a potential future growth driver beyond the current commercial product. Completing enrollment on schedule would improve development visibility and could broaden Protalix’s rare-disease pipeline if efficacy and safety support later-stage advancement.

bear.b: Dependence on Chiesi purchasing patterns makes reported revenue less predictable than recurring end-demand alone would suggest. Uneven shipments and inventory decisions can create volatility in quarterly results, complicating forecasting and making sustained commercial momentum harder to assess.

The large milestone materially boosted first-half revenue but is not expected to recur, reducing the quality and comparability of near-term growth. Future performance will therefore depend more heavily on recurring Elfabrio sales and partner activity than headline H1 figures imply.

The observed immunogenicity rate and unresolved dosing choice create meaningful uncertainty for PRX-115’s development path. Antidrug antibodies and infusion-related reactions could affect regimen selection, timelines, clinical differentiation, and ultimately the program’s commercial positioning.
